$$Q_{\text{lost by brass}} = Q_{\text{gained by aluminium}}$$

Using $Q = m\,c\,\Delta T$ for each side, where $\Delta T$ is the change in temperature:

$$m_b c_b (T_b - T_f) = m_a c_a (T_f - T_a)$$

Now plug in the values — brass loses heat, so its temperature change is $(200 - T_f)$, and aluminium gains heat, so its change is $(T_f - 20)$:

$$600(0.39)(200 - T_f) = 400(0.90)(T_f - 20)$$

Simplifying the coefficients gives:

$$234(200 - T_f) = 360(T_f - 20)$$

Expanding:

$$46{,}800 - 234T_f = 360T_f - 7200$$

Gathering like terms:

$$46{,}800 + 7200 = 360T_f + 234T_f$$

$$54{,}000 = 594T_f$$

$$T_f = \frac{54{,}000}{594} = 90.9\,^\circ\text{C}$$

So the final temperature of the mixture is **90.9 °C**.
